purpose: Amikacin is a powerful antibiotic used to treat serious bacterial infections, especially those caused by bacteria that are resistant to other antibiotics. It is commonly used for infections of the lungs, blood, urinary tract, skin, bones, and abdomen. Doctors often prescribe it in the hospital for severe or hard-to-treat infections.
how_it_works: Amikacin works by getting inside harmful bacteria and blocking their ability to make the proteins they need to survive and grow. Without these proteins, the bacteria cannot function and eventually die off. Think of it like removing a key machine from a factory — the factory simply cannot keep running.
common_side_effects: The most important side effects to watch for are hearing problems (like ringing in the ears or difficulty hearing), dizziness or balance issues, and decreased kidney function. You may also notice pain or irritation at the injection site. Not everyone experiences these, but it is important to tell your healthcare team right away if anything feels off.
warnings: Amikacin can cause serious damage to your kidneys and hearing, especially with higher doses or longer use — these effects can sometimes be permanent. Your doctor will regularly check your kidney function and drug levels in your blood to keep you safe. Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, have kidney disease, or are taking other medications that affect the kidneys. Never take more than prescribed.
typical_dosing: Amikacin is given as an injection into a vein (IV) or into a muscle — it is not available as a pill you take at home. In adults, a common dose is 15 mg per kg of body weight once daily, though your doctor will adjust this based on your weight, kidney function, and the type of infection. Treatment usually lasts 7 to 10 days, and your blood levels will be monitored closely throughout.
